native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: Social psychology (the `Social` discipline — the social/personality-psychology domain dominated by the Reproducibility Project: Psychology pairs, plus the social-psychology effects of Many Labs 1 and 3) is the domain in which both the original and the replication studies primarily used student subjects. In these 74 O/R pairs 62/73 = 84.9% of originals and 60/73 = 82.2% of replications used student subjects at the study level (83.6%/80.6% when the four repeated titles are collapsed, 82.2%/78.6% across all lab-level rows), a pair that brackets the quoted 82.4%/80.9% and is the closest match of any domain under 6 of the 7 analytic conventions tested. Cognitive psychology (75.5% original vs 81.6% replication) and experimental economics (94.4% vs 100%) fail to show the same near-82%/near-81% combination. Within Social the only departure from student samples is on the replication side (3 studies moved from student to online samples, plus anyone/community samples), and the `online` subject type exists only in replications (0 originals vs 148 replication rows), so the original-to-replication decline reflects a shift in sampling mode rather than in the target population.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded both staged CSVs (File A 927x57 with 141 unique O/R ids; File B 143x15). 2) Join diagnostics showed File B has no subject column and no usable key (0/143 exact study==authors.o, 83/143 surname matches, 0/31 Experimental Philosophy studies in File A), so File B was excluded and the limitation reported. 3) Built the headline study-level frame: the 26 aggregated==True roll-up rows (ml1/ml3) + the 115 non-aggregated rpp/ee rows = 141 unique ids, asserted. 4) Derived a robustness `field` variable from `journal`/title (social-personality, cognitive, economics, political science/public opinion, Psych Science, judgment & decision, general science). 5) For every candidate category computed n studies, students.o n/%, students.r n/% over denominator = non-missing subject coding, plus deviation |pct_o-82.4|+|pct_r-80.9|; ranked discipline, project and journal-derived field in one table. 6) Re-ran the same statistics under 7 conventions (headline; missing-as-non-student; unique-title dedup; lab-row level 927; lab rows excluding aggregated; modal lab-row subject code; drop==True excluded) and recorded each category's range and best deviation. 7) Ran an exhaustive 1-2-column grouping search (17 fields x 4 row bases, min group size 8, 3251 candidate categories) to test whether any category reproduces 82.4/80.9; the closest hits were non-domain procedural intersections, reported as evidence that the source table used an undocumented convention rather than used as the answer. 8) Inspected within-category detail for Social and for runner-up rpp (subject-type distributions, o->r transitions, list of non-student studies, online-only-in-replications fact). 9) Wrote out/headline_categories.csv, out/sensitivity_table.csv, out/exhaustive_grouping_search.csv, out/social_discipline_studies.csv, out/analysis_log.txt and out/REPORT.md.

sub_hypo.text: Within Social psychology, the decline in student sampling from original to replication studies reflects a shift in sampling mode rather than in the target population.
sub_hypo.context: Within-pair subject-type transitions in Social-discipline studies in File A, with the online-only-in-replications observation assessed across all File A lab-level rows.
sub_hypo.relations: The hypothesis locates departures from student sampling on the replication side: three Social studies moved from student to online samples, alongside anyone/community replication samples.
